title: Turn the table, lose the wobble
hook: Can a turn help this square equal-leg table?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts

Square equal-leg table, continuous ground and slope/leg length conditions; proof of sign change and balanced position. Our cosine gap is an illustration, not a solution of the full contact geometry.

claims.text: Four feet down is not level. Clear hot drinks before turning; steps, holes and unequal legs fall outside this model.

claims.text: Recall: A square equal-leg table on gentle continuous ground has four feet touching after a turn. What has been established? Correct answer: All four feet contact the ground; the top may still slope. Contact means the feet touch the ground. It does not mean the tabletop is level. Equal legs and suitably gentle continuous ground belong to the stated model; unequal legs fall outside it.
